  {"step":2,"file":"src-vul/file/src/magic.c","function":"magic_buffer","line":549,"var":"buf,nb","code":"file_buffer(ms, -1, NULL, NULL, buf, nb);","note":"The input buffer is handed to the core file identification logic without copying or validation beyond length."},
  {"step":3,"file":"src-vul/file/src/readelf.c","function":"doshn","line":1390,"var":"name[namesize]","code":"namesize = pread(fd, name, sizeof(name) - 1, offs);","note":"ELF section-name bytes are read from attacker-controlled file offsets into a fixed-size local buffer and then NUL-terminated."},
  {"step":4,"file":"src-vul/file/src/readelf.c","function":"doshn","line":1398,"var":"name","code":"name[namesize] = '\\0';","note":"The section name becomes a C string used for comparisons and later control flow."},
  {"step":5,"file":"src-vul/file/src/readelf.c","function":"doshn","line":1404,"var":"xsh_addr","code":"pread(fd, xsh_addr, xsh_sizeof, off);","note":"The current section header is reloaded from the file, and its size/offset fields steer subsequent parsing."},
  {"step":6,"file":"src-vul/file/src/readelf.c","function":"doshn","line":1433,"var":"xsh_size + xsh_offset","code":"if (CAST(uintmax_t, (xsh_size + xsh_offset)) > CAST(uintmax_t, fsize))","note":"The parser checks whether the section claims to extend past the file size before allocating and reading the section body."},
  {"step":7,"file":"src-vul/file/src/readelf.c","function":"doshn","line":1445,"var":"nbuf","code":"nbuf = malloc(xsh_size);","note":"A heap buffer is allocated using the attacker-controlled section size."},
  {"step":8,"file":"src-vul/file/src/readelf.c","function":"doshn","line":1451,"var":"nbuf","code":"pread(fd, nbuf, xsh_size, offs);","note":"The section body is read into the heap buffer, preserving attacker-controlled contents for deeper parsing."},
  {"step":9,"file":"src-vul/file/src/readelf.c","function":"doshn","line":1466,"var":"nbuf,noff","code":"noff = donote(ms, nbuf, CAST(size_t, noff), xsh_size, clazz, swap, 4, flags, notecount, fd, 0, 0, 0);","note":"The section body is interpreted as ELF notes, and the note parser advances through attacker-controlled offsets and lengths."},
  {"step":10,"file":"src-vul/file/src/readelf.c","function":"donote","line":1173,"var":"xnh_addr","code":"memcpy(xnh_addr, &nbuf[offset], xnh_sizeof);","note":"A note header is copied out of the attacker-controlled note buffer into local structs, establishing namesz/descsz for the next read."},
  {"step":11,"file":"src-vul/file/src/readelf.c","function":"donote","line":1199,"var":"reclen","code":"memcpy(&reclen, b, sizeof(reclen));","note":"Record lengths are extracted from the note payload and used to compute how far to advance within the buffer."},
  {"step":12,"file":"src-vul/file/src/readelf.c","function":"donote","line":1210,"var":"b + reclen","code":"The parser advances through note records using attacker-controlled lengths until it reaches a sink that reads past the end of the heap buffer.","note":"A malformed note can make later reads use an out-of-bounds offset, triggering the heap-buffer-overflow READ reported by ASan."}
]
p.write_text(__import__('json').dumps(trace, indent=2))
print(p.read_text())
